info.title: Research API
info.description:
The Research API provides on-demand access to Morningstar’s repository of equity and fund research. 
 [Research on thousands of global companies and managed products](https://www.morningstar.com/products/research) is available, as well as thematic research spanning entire sectors or industry groups.</br></br>
 **Note:** The API provides access to research content in PDF or Excel file
 format. If you require research content packaged as JSON or XML, you can use
 the Research Publishing System API service.


 
 **Equity Research Endpoints**</br></br>
 Requests to the `equity` endpoints of the Research API return the following research
 documents:

   * Company Report (PDF)
   * Company Valuation Model (Excel)
   * Moat Framework Report (PDF)
   * Quantitative Company Report (PDF)
   * Enhanced Quantitative Company Report (PDF)     
   * Stock Analyst Notes (PDF)
   * Thematic Research (PDF)

 **Fund Research Endpoints**</br></br>
 Requests to the `fund` endpoints of the Research API return the following reports: 

   * Carbon Report (PDF)
   * Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Report (PDF)
   * Managed Investment Report (PDF)
   * Target-Date Series Report (PDF)

 **Requests**</br>
 
 Reports are updated throughout the day, so to ensure that you always have the most up-to-date version, you should make a new request every time you want to download a report.</br></br>

 **Response**</br>
 A URL returned in the response is used to access the document file (PDF or
 Excel). You should not cache this URL because the link expires within a few
 minutes.

get.description:
Get the **most recent** version of a company-related report for the company specified in the `companyIdentifier` parameter. You can identify a company using a performance ID (for example,`0P00012BBI`)  or `exchange:ticker` value, (for example, `XNAS:GOOG`). </br></br>  The following document types can be retrieved using this endpoint:
  </br></br> - Company Report</br> - Stock Analyst Note</br>- Valuation Model</br>- Thematic Research</br></br>A URL returned in the response is used to access the document file.
  </br></br>**Note** To get current and historical company-related research documents, use
  the **equity - rps document** endpoints.

parameters.name: companyIdentifier
parameters.description: Unique identifier of a company. Valid values are performance ID or `exchange:ticker` value.

parameters.name: reportType
parameters.description: Type of report

parameters.name: reportView
parameters.description: View of report. Currently, only `latest` is supported.

get.summary: Get a Research Publishing System (RPS) document
get.description: Get the Research Publishing System (RPS) document specifed in the `documentId` parameter. You can use this endpoint to retrieve current and historical company research documents.</br></br>**Note** The three **equity - rps document** endpoints return almost the same content. In addition to the content also returned by the other two endpoints, this endpoint must be used for Thematic Research documents, as this research is not associated with any specific company. We recommend you use this endpoint as it is the simplest and returns all document types including thematic research.</br></br>The following document types can be retrieved using this endpoint: </br></br> - Company Report</br> - Stock Analyst Note</br>- Valuation Model</br>- Thematic Research</br></br>A URL returned in the response is used to access the document file.

get.description: Get a Quantitative Report for the company specified in the `companyIdentifier` parameter. Quantitative Reports provide a detailed assessment of a company based on a quantitative analysis using a variety of company financial data and other data inputs. </br></br>You can identify a company using a performance ID (for example,`0P00012BBI`)  or `exchange:ticker` value, (for example, `XNAS:GOOG`). </br></br>To override the default value in the Accept-Language HTTP header, use the `locale` parameter. </br></br>In the `pageSize` parameter, you can specify the page size for the returned PDF. Page size options are `Letter` or `A4`.</br></br> A URL returned in the response is used to access the document file.

get.description:
Get an Carbon Report for the fund specified in the `FundIdentifier` parameter.</br></br>
 Carbon Reports provide an investment level analysis of a fund’s carbon risk. The report uses Morningstar’s Portfolio Carbon Metrics to provide an overview of how well a portfolio is managing transition risk and other key 
 carbon-related information, such as carbon intensity and fossil fuel exposure. You can use these metrics to identify and evaluate lower carbon-risk alternatives to funds or assess how well sustainable funds meet their stated mandates.
</br></br>In the `pageSize` parameter, you can specify the page size for the returned PDF. Page size options are `Letter` or `A4`.</br></br>If a report exists, a presigned URL from which you can download the PDF is returned in the response.
